A1.justification: Both PDFs describe macOSWorld and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A-G. These materials align reliably; v4 additionally appends a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: v3 reports original agent evaluations, human task-completion measurements, safety-attack outcomes, cross-language experiments and SoM comparisons (Figure 3, Section 5 and Appendix D).

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the six-agent benchmark, safety evaluation and supplementary experiments.

M1.justification: The benchmark pipeline, interactive pop-up attacks and Appendix G agent procedures remain unchanged. Appendix B's new watermarking suggestion is not incorporated into the implemented method.

E1.justification: Both retain 202 English tasks, the same language-dependent subsets across five languages, 30-application coverage, 29 English safety tasks and the same cross-language scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches within every corresponding experiment: the six agents in Tables 3 and 5, OpenAI CUA's cross-language comparisons, and GPT-4o with and without SoM in Table 8.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains the 1024×768 environment, 15-screenshot/30-turn limits, recent-screenshot context settings and binary success-rate evaluation. Model versions and supplementary experimental protocols also match.

E4.justification: The SoM ablation, language-mismatch analysis, human timing analysis, safety tests and detailed failure cases are retained unchanged (Figure 3, Section 5 and Appendices D-E).

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, uncertainty estimates or significance tests for agent performance. Added checklist item 7 acknowledges this absence without changing the reporting practice.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 3 retains Claude/OpenAI CUA average success rates of 37.1%/33.8%, and Table 5 retains their distraction rates of 72.4%/69.0%; supplementary results also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 retains the same POMDP formulation, state-transition description and binary-reward definition. No theorems, proofs or new mathematical reasoning are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same multilingual macOS benchmark and safety contributions, alongside unchanged claims about performance tiers, language disparities and deception vulnerability.

C2.justification: Appendix B adds output watermarking as a possible aid to auditability and traceability, supplementing the existing isolation and snapshot-restoration discussion. Failure-mechanism interpretations and the binary-reward limitation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces its direct repository link with a project-page access route, repeated in the new checklist. The checklist also adds an LLM-use declaration; existing hardware, model versions, prompts and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Four references are added for Appendix B's safeguarding suggestion: RingID, WMAdapter, Can Simple Averaging Defeat Modern Watermarks?, and IDProtector. Existing GUI-agent and benchmark positioning is unchanged; other citation shifts are renumberings.

P1.justification: v4 appends a 16-item NeurIPS checklist, adds a funding acknowledgement and updates publication and project-access text. The existing narrative and appendices remain almost verbatim, without substantial rewriting or reorganization.

P2.justification: All 20 figures and nine tables retain their content and designs. Changes are limited to typesetting and reflow around the front matter, references and Appendix B/Figure 5, plus the appended checklist layout.

improvement.justification: The benchmark, empirical evidence and detailed implementation instructions remain unchanged. The checklist largely repeats existing disclosures, while the access-link update, funding acknowledgement and tentative watermarking suggestion provide peripheral documentation changes without materially improving or harming overall paper quality.
